conventions.convention: AC is assumed throughout the batch, including inherited algebraic dimension, topology and constructible derived-category constructions.

Coefficients are an arbitrary field; constructible complexes are cohomologically bounded with finite-rank locally constant cohomology on finite algebraic strata. The cohomological shift satisfies H^j(A[m]) = H^{j+m}(A).

The distance exhaustion is on a closed affine algebraic embedding. Good centers exist in every prescribed nonempty real parameter open; critical points are finite but their critical values need not be distinct.
The tangent Morse index λ is real. Normal relative cochains are Cone(A_p → RΓ(L,A|L))[-1], and total local relative cochains are the normal complex shifted by -λ. An empty link has zero cochains.

For nonpure spaces, d may be an upper complex dimension. At an s-dimensional stratum the link has upper dimension d-s-1. A collared ball-cut link is handled through its open-cut logarithmic exhaustion, rather than being treated as a closed affine variety.

Smooth relative-d pullback is normalized by [d]; transverse complex codimension-c pullback by [-c]. Complex orientation gives a^! = a^*[2d] and i^!P = i^*P[-2c], with the embedding comparison restricted to complexes constructible for the transverse stratification.

For affine u, Ru_* preserves the upper perverse aisle and Ru_! preserves the lower aisle. The affine-open characterization is an iff, testing every affine Zariski open and every positive cohomological degree.

The defect is max(2i + dim Y_i - dim X) over nonempty fibre-dimension loci. The universal incidence source has dimension n+d-1. Smallness means defect zero with strictly negative contributions for positive fibre dimensions; empty fixed sections are omitted.

The universal-family embedding has d ≥ 1 and M = i^*p'^*K[d-1]. Restriction is an isomorphism for l ≤ -2 and monic at -1; Gysin is an isomorphism for l ≥ 2 and epic at 1. Largest base subobjects and quotients refer to the essential image of p^*[d].

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, at a nondegenerate stratified critical point on an s-dimensional complex stratum, local relative constructible cochains are the normal relative complex shifted by -λ; the normal complex is Cone(A_p → RΓ(L,A|L))[-1]. For a proper strongly plurisubharmonic stratified Morse exhaustion with finitely many critical points, critical-value relative cochains are finite direct sums of these complexes, and regular bands preserve constructible cohomology. Collared algebraic ball-cut links admit the stated finite-critical logarithmic exhaustion.

Assuming inherited AC, an algebraically constructible finite-dimensional field sheaf on a complex affine variety has H^q = 0 above the dimension of the closure of its support. Upper perverse aisle objects have H^q = 0 for q > 0; lower aisle objects have H_c^q = 0 for q < 0. Empty varieties and zero coefficients give zero groups.

Assuming inherited AC, for an affine morphism u of complex algebraic varieties, Ru_* preserves the upper perverse aisle and Ru_! preserves the lower aisle. A bounded constructible K belongs to the upper aisle iff H^q(V,K) = 0 for every affine Zariski open V and every q > 0.

Assume AC. For a closed algebraic Z in complex affine space with a finite smooth algebraic Whitney stratification, every prescribed nonempty real parameter open contains a center a such that squared distance to a is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion, has finitely many nondegenerate stratum critical points, and at each critical point its ambient differential kills no limiting tangent plane of another approaching stratum. Critical values may coincide.

Assuming inherited AC, smooth pure relative-complex-dimension-d pullback a^*[d] is perverse-exact and a^! = a^*[2d]. For a restriction of a smooth complex closed embedding of codimension c transverse to every stratum, i^*[-c] is perverse-exact and i^!P ≅ i^*P[-2c] for complexes constructible for that stratification.

Assuming inherited AC, for a projective f:X→Y with a closed embedding X→P^d, d≥1, and perverse K, the universal-family object M=i^*p'^*K[d-1] is perverse. Restriction gives p^*pH^l(Rf_*K)[d]→pH^{l+1}(Rg_*M), isomorphic for l≤-2 and monic for l=-1, with dual Gysin isomorphisms for l≥2 and epimorphism for l=1. The pullbacks of pH^{-1}(Rf_*K) and pH^1(Rf_*K), shifted by d, are respectively the largest base pullback subobject and quotient of pH^0(Rg_*M).

Assuming inherited AC, for a projective map of complex projective varieties with smooth nonempty irreducible source and a fixed embedding into P^d, d≥1, the universal incidence map has defect at most r(f)-1 when r(f)>0 and is small when r(f)=0. A nonempty Zariski open of fixed hyperplanes gives smooth sections with the same conclusions; empty sections are omitted.

seams_checked.note: Checked the constructible six-operation and ordinary middle-perverse suppliers against the uses of duality, support inequalities, finite length, negative Hom, proper base change and smooth orientation. The batch retains arbitrary field coefficients and AC; it does not import semisimplicity or a decomposition theorem from these suppliers.

Checked the Whitney/control definitions, controlled-submersion products, compact triangulations and finite conical models against the exhaustion and Morse constructions. Compact real wall families have explicit transversality and properness checks; coefficient transport is separately constructed. Ball-cut links retain their collar and logarithmic-exhaustion qualification. The codimension induction and tangent-index bound also agree with [Goresky, §§17.2 and 17.7–17.9](https://www.math.ias.edu/~goresky/pdf/all2.pdf).

Checked the joint projective induction's relevant facts and constructions: positive-defect source cuts, universal-family weak Lefschetz, maximal pullback objects, normalized noncharacteristic specialization, and compact-support Artin for target weak Lefschetz. Its Thom/cup identity is constructed separately rather than attributed to the universal-family supplier. Degrees and hypotheses agree with the assigned statements and [de Cataldo–Migliorini, §4.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0306030).
